title: 90% of US working hours are spent on tasks not covered well by AI benchmarks
titleZh: 美国 90% 的工作时间都花在了人工智能基准未涵盖的任务上
author: speckx
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: b800h
comments.textRawHtml: Perhaps a version of the Doorman Fallacy, ie. replacing a doorman with an automatic door seems like an obvious win, but it turns out the doorman was performing a number of other vital functions (customer experience, for example) which weren't considered.
comments.textZhHtml: 也许是门卫谬误的一个版本，即。用自动门取代门卫似乎是一个明显的胜利，但事实证明门卫正在执行许多其他未被考虑的重要功能（例如客户体验）。

children.author: etempleton
children.textRawHtml:
This has been my argument for the past few weeks to explain why we aren’t seeing or feeling real world productivity gains as consumers despite many espousing the efficiency of AI they personally see with their own workflows. The hands on work is rarely the actual bottleneck.

My team can crank out high quality work in a few hours and AI could do the same medium to high quality work in a minute or two, but the review, feedback, and sign off takes days of back and forth. AI just slows this part of the process down because editing AI work is often a challenge because, no one is quite as familiar with how it was put together and sometimes it creates things that are not editable at all. And telling AI to make very specific changes is often a mixed bag at best.

Solo devs and small teams with minimal oversight can probably move a lot faster, but corporations are going to see minimal uplift except in areas where no one is looking.
children.textZhHtml:
这一直是我在过去几周的论点，以解释为什么我们作为消费者没有看到或感受到现实世界的生产力提高，尽管许多人拥护他们亲眼所见的人工智能在自己的工作流程中的效率。动手工作很少是真正的瓶颈。

我的团队可以在几个小时内完成高质量的工作，人工智能可以在一两分钟内完成相同的中等到高质量的工作，但审查、反馈和签署需要几天的时间来回。人工智能只是减慢了这部分过程，因为编辑人工智能工作通常是一项挑战，因为没有人非常熟悉它是如何组合在一起的，有时它会创建根本无法编辑的东西。告诉人工智能做出非常具体的改变往往是一个好坏参半的问题。

独立开发者和监督最少的小团队可能会移动得更快，但除了无人关注的领域之外，企业将看到最小的提升。

children.author: majormajor
children.textRawHtml:
Established successful companies operate in a world where action and change often introduce more immediate risk than staying still. In those companies AI doesn't necessarily offer a lot of "increased productivity" gains because writing the code isn't the bottleneck. But many of them will try to chase cost savings by laying people off or slowing hiring.

There's a couple types of companies where the reverse is true: young companies trying to grow, and dying ones that need a turnaround.

Out of those two, young companies are less likely to be set in their ways. So the first place you really see the result of development moving faster with AI is probably going to be in future months and years when suddenly-big companies start getting widely known with products and business strategies that wouldn't have made sense a decade ago because writing code to try different things to even get the ball rolling was a bottleneck, and you could only do things that wouldn't scale for so long.
children.textZhHtml:
对于成熟的成功公司来说，行动和变革往往比保持静止会带来更直接的风险。在这些公司中，人工智能不一定会带来很多“提高生产力”的收益，因为编写代码并不是瓶颈。但他们中的许多人会试图通过裁员或放慢招聘速度来节省成本。

有几种类型的公司情况恰恰相反：年轻的公司试图发展，而垂死的公司需要扭亏为盈。

在这两种公司中，年轻的公司不太可能按自己的方式行事。因此，你第一个真正看到 AI 带来的更快发展的结果可能是在未来的几个月和几年里，那时大公司突然开始以十年前没有意义的产品和业务策略而广为人知，因为编写代码来尝试不同的事情甚至让事情滚动是一个瓶颈，你只能做一些无法长期扩展的事情。

children.author: dingdongditchme
children.textRawHtml: Or the productivity gains, albeit substantial, are not as earth shattering as the llm providers would have you believe. As with any new technology adoption is a laggard. The internet "existed" in the late 80's, early 90's. Many companies are still reaping productivity gains from plugging into this first.
children.textZhHtml: 或者说，生产力的提高虽然很大，但并不像法学硕士提供商让您相信的那样是惊天动地的。与任何新技术一样，采用都是落后的。互联网“存在”于20世纪80年代末90年代初。许多公司仍然通过首先介入这一领域来获得生产力的提高。

children.author: lumost
children.textRawHtml:
I work in code generation, and often feel the fallacy of “because I can build something that looks 80% like your product in a day, you should pay me N millions.”

It's roughly the same pitch that the ruby on rails crowd had 15 years ago, and the no code crowd 5 years ago.

Very few companies need to rebuild their product every week, or actually care what tech stack it runs on. They are trying to build new things, or reduce how often those things break, or figuring out what if anything is worth building next.
children.textZhHtml:
我从事代码生成工作，经常感到这样的谬论：“因为我可以在一天内构建出与您的产品看起来 80% 相似的东西，您应该付给我 N 百万美元。”

这与 15 年前的 Ruby on Rails 人群和 5 年前的无代码人群的宣传大致相同。

很少有公司需要每周重建他们的产品，或者真正关心什么技术堆栈它继续运行。他们正在尝试构建新的事物，或者减少这些事物损坏的频率，或者弄清楚下一步是否值得构建什么。

children.author: thelastgallon
children.textRawHtml:
> Solo devs and small teams with minimal oversight can probably move a lot faster

Spot on!

Usually, most work in corps is slowed down by executive decisions. It takes 3 - 9 months to get a yes/no on something and for most things that are obvious that need to be done need to go up the chain of command. The decision takes forever, but when the decision is made, they want things to be done quickly, which creates unreasonable stress on the ICs.

The first step to see real productivity gains is for AI to eliminate the executive and middle-management layer, this starts a virtuous cycle, destroys both empire building and massively accelerates true productivity, not just meaningless metrics like LOC.
children.textZhHtml:
> 单独的开发人员和监督最少的小团队可能会进展得更快

完全正确！

通常，团队中的大多数工作都会因执行决策而减慢。需要 3 - 9 个月的时间才能对某件事做出是/否的决定，对于大多数明显需要完成的事情，都需要向上级指挥。决策需要很长时间，但当决策做出后，他们希望事情能够快速完成，这对 IC 造成了不合理的压力。

看到真正生产力提升的第一步是人工智能消除执行层和中层管理层，这会启动一个良性循环，破坏帝国建设并大幅加速真正的生产力，而不仅仅是像 LOC 这样毫无意义的指标。

children.author: somenameforme
children.textRawHtml:
Speaking realistically, you're going in the wrong direction here. The most likely scenario in the short run is that management will seek to replace labor with automated systems supported by a skeleton crew to aid in implementation and execution level tasks that can't (or shouldn't) be handled by the LLM alone, like deployment.

So the first signs of productivity gains will be shrinking head count, but it's going go from the bottom up, as usual.
children.textZhHtml:
说实话，你在这里走错了方向。短期内最有可能的情况是，管理层将寻求用由骨干人员支持的自动化系统取代劳动力，以帮助实施和执行级别的任务，这些任务不能（或不应该）由法学硕士单独处理，例如部署。

因此，生产力提高的第一个迹象将是减少员工人数，但它会像往常一样从下到上进行。

children.author: abustamam
children.textRawHtml:
I considered it an absolute win when I submitted an LLM assisted PR that removed 30k LOC :)

> most work in corps is slowed down by executive decisions

I work in a startup and I find it to be the opposite. Management wants us to go really fast and engineering is like "well wait we should slow down because just because LLMs can write a bunch of code doesn't mean it can build a maintainable app"

That said, I know that our small engineering team can't build an entire business by ourselves. So some management is required. But as you said, getting stuff done quickly is stressful. And with LLMs we're expected to get a LOT of stuff done very quickly. Some colleagues have decided to go on quiet strike by submitting AI slop and citing "no time to review" to prove a point. I don't fault them, but I also know that me and someone else will have to clean up their messes at some point.
children.textZhHtml:
当我提交了一份 LLM 辅助 PR 并删除了 30k LOC 时，我认为这是绝对的胜利:)

> 团队中的大多数工作都因执行决策而减慢

我在一家初创公司工作，我发现情况恰恰相反。管理层希望我们走得非常快，而工程就像“好吧，我们应该放慢速度，因为法学硕士可以编写一堆代码并不意味着它可以构建一个可维护的应用程序”

也就是说，我知道我们的小型工程团队无法独自构建整个业务。所以需要一些管理。但正如你所说，快速完成工作会带来压力。通过法学硕士，我们预计能够很快完成很多工作。一些同事决定以“没有时间审查”为由，通过提交人工智能废液来证明这一点，从而进行安静的罢工。我不会责怪他们，但我也知道我和其他人在某个时候必须清理他们的烂摊子。

children.author: wookmaster
children.textRawHtml:
They way these companies are structured we're seeing them remove the people doing the actual work while nobody wants to mess with the execs. My company has something like 60 EVP titles, with SVPs then VPs then senior director then directors. Pretty much everyone VP and above could disappear and our lives would be easier. It creates a lot of politickings and empire building that holds back the company and the individuals then the individuals delivering code and products get targeted by the efficiency metrics and nothing at the top changes.

I have no idea how it’s sustainable but I dont see AI CEOs coming until a new company becomes successful from the bottom using that model.

children.author: leftouterjoins
children.textRawHtml:
This is my experience. As a data engineer with years in my current role I can get AI to write good SQL that correctly answers questions or defines metrics. At worst it may take a few back and forths to really nail it.

However, if a PM tries it they will more often than not get a wrong answer because they do not know what to look for or how to ask the right questions.

Prompts still matter a lot especially when you are working in an established enterprise.
children.textZhHtml:
这是我的经验。作为一名在当前职位上工作多年的数据工程师，我可以让 AI 编写出良好的 SQL 来正确回答问题或定义指标。在最坏的情况下，可能需要反复几次才能真正解决问题。

但是，如果产品经理尝试这样做，他们往往会得到错误的答案，因为他们不知道要寻找什么或如何提出正确的问题。

提示仍然很重要，尤其是当您在成熟的企业中工作时。

children.author: weinzierl
children.textRawHtml:
I know the Doorman Fallacy is an established concept, but where did it really ever apply? The automatic door has won despite, devastatingly so (and no your fancy upper east side building doesn't count and neither does the Regency or the Hilton).

The doorman was called a doorman because its essential task was the door. Everything else was additional and replaceable or unnecessary in the first place.

Same with AI. Once it has replaced the main task, the rest will adapt around it.
children.textZhHtml:
我知道门卫谬误是一个既定的概念，但它真正适用于哪里？尽管如此，自动门还是取得了毁灭性的胜利（不，你那精美的上东区建筑不算在内，摄政酒店或希尔顿酒店也不算在内）。

门卫被称为门卫，因为它的基本任务是门。首先，其他一切都是额外的、可替换的或不必要的。

人工智能也是如此。一旦它取代了主要任务，其余的就会围绕它进行调整。

children.author: CodeyWhizzBang
children.textRawHtml:
When you say the automatic door "has won" do you mean it's won by rendering doormen obsolete? Because if so, that seems very untrue. According to Vanity Fair and NPR there are over 25,000 doormen working in New York City. 1930 there were an estimated few thousand. So since the invention of the automatic door, the number of doormen has skyrocketed.

Maybe, you'd say there are more automatic doors than doormen. I'm confident that is true, but those automatic doors haven't supplanted doormen; they're automatic doors where there would have been manual doors before.

So everything hasn't adapted around automatic doors. We've just got a lot more automatic doors now. And a lot more doormen.
children.textZhHtml:
当您说自动门“获胜”时，您的意思是通过淘汰门卫而赢得胜利吗？因为如果是这样，那就显得非常不真实了。据 Vanity Fair 和 NPR 报道，纽约市有超过 25,000 名门卫。 1930 年估计有几千人。所以自从自动门发明以来，门卫的数量猛增。

也许，你会说自动门比门卫还多。我相信这是真的，但那些自动门并没有取代门卫；它们是自动门，以前有手动门。

所以一切都还没有适应自动门。我们现在有了更多的自动门。还有更多的门卫。

children.author: philipov
children.textRawHtml:
You can't only compare doormen to doormen, because the number of people and doors have increased too. You need to compare doormen to doors. All the apartment buildings I've known people live at on Manhattan have only had automatic doors. You need to show that automatic doors replaced unguarded doors.

1) What proportion of doors had doormen before compared to now?

2) What proportion of the population was employed as doormen then and now?

3) What proportion of the population benefited from doormen then and now?

children.author: CodeyWhizzBang
children.textRawHtml:
I don't think that's necessary to refute the original point. The point I was disagreeing with was that automatic doors have "won" and doormen are no longer relevant. Whether 25,000 is a higher proportion of New Yorkers now than it was in 1930 isn't really a key point. 25,000 remains a large enough number that it is not true that doormen have been wiped out.

That said, to your actual points, as an intellectual exercise: while the population of New York has increased since 1930 (from around 7m to around 9m), the number of doormen has gone up much much faster (from "a few thousand" according to NPR to 25,000). So on the criteria you listed there, the number of doormen has increased as well.

The doorman example remains true.
children.textZhHtml:
我认为没有必要反驳原来的观点。我不同意的一点是，自动门已经“获胜”，门卫不再相关。 25,000 人现在的纽约人比例是否比 1930 年更高并不是真正的关键点。 25,000 人仍然是一个足够大的数字，因此门卫已被消灭的说法并不属实。

也就是说，就你的实际观点而言，作为一项智力练习：虽然纽约人口自 1930 年以来一直在增加（从约 700 万增加到约 900 万），但门卫的数量增长得更快（根据 NPR 的报道，从“几千人”增加到 25,000 人）。因此，根据您在那里列出的标准，门卫的数量也增加了。

门卫的例子仍然正确。
